per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window for apo loop L13 V308-V322 (S2 0.53, τs about 1 ns, 25 °C; J7, r3); the rest of the apo backbone averages S2 0.85 with lower values in loops L1 and L12. The TSA complex is more ordered (average S2 0.91; only residue 112 and the C-terminus stand out; J23, r16), and its L13 amides are broadened out (J22, r17, r24).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window. Apo WT at 25 °C (citrate pH 6.5): four backbone clusters, NTD hinge kex 1,930 s-1 / pB 0.4%, interface 800 s-1 / 1.1%, dynamic domain 1 790 or 990 s-1 (inconsistent within the paper), loop L8 790 s-1 / 2.6% (J1-J5, r1, r2). The 2011 four-temperature fit gives interface 570-1,440 s-1 and L8 530-1,080 s-1 with L8 pB 3.5-5.7% from 15 to 30 °C (J8, J9, r4-r7); hinge and core-sheet multi-temperature fits did not converge. Apo methyls at 25 °C: 6 of 71 ILV exchange, L8-adjacent methyls at 970 s-1 / 4.8%, dynamic-domain-1 methyls at 3,890 s-1 / 0.56%, I210 suggesting three states (J10-J14, r11). Model-free Rex terms in about 35% of residues are unconfirmed (J6). Bound states at 25 °C in imidazole/Mg buffer: MCA 914 s-1 / 3.1% (J17, r12); TSA methyls 4,247 s-1 (J18, r13) and TSA backbone 2,300-2,750 s-1 in two collective groups with 77 Rex residues (J20, J21, r15); PCA 4,690 s-1 (J19, r14).
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for apo WT (J16); no CEST, ZZ-exchange, HDX, EPR or FRET rows. kclose 19-62 s-1 (r4-r7) and MCA kAB 28 s-1 (r12) are directional rates inside the millisecond processes.
per_window.undetermined: Apo RDCs fit a 0.5-0.7 apo/TSA mixture but cannot separate a static average from exchange (J15, r8, r9). Apo-versus-TSA crystals (J24), ambient TSA crystals (J25), noncognate-analogue closures (J26) and the C271A mutant (J27) are structure_only or mutant inference. Homolog rows (Daphnia in phosphate, spider crystals and MD, lobster SAXS; J28-J31) never decide the WT verdict. Not judged: r35 and r40 (E314D/E225Q mutant structures, abstract only), r31 (DFT cluster model, no protein dynamics), r32 and r39 (abstract-only TSA endpoints), r37 (creatine kinase versus AK cross-protein comparison).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 25 °C substrate-free wild-type Limulus arginine kinase (10 mM citrate, pH 6.5, no buffer control) exchanges on the microsecond-millisecond scale in four backbone regions, the N-terminal-domain hinge D88-G92 (kex 1,930 ± 350 s-1, pB 0.4%), the domain interface (800 ± 100 s-1, pB 1.1%), the dynamic-domain-1 hinge (790 ± 70 s-1 in Table 1, 990 ± 110 s-1 in the text) and loop L8 I182-G209 (790 ± 60 s-1, pB 2.6 ± 0.6%). A 2011 four-temperature fit of the same regions gives rates rising from about 530-570 s-1 at 15 °C to 1,080-1,440 s-1 at 30 °C, with an L8 minor state of 3.5-5.7% estimated from three residues.
open_conflicts: Loop L8 population at 25 °C, apo (model/subset difference, not a data conflict): the 2009 collective fit of all 17 L8 residues gives pB 2.6 ± 0.6% (r1), while the 2011 fit takes pB from only the three slow-intermediate residues E190, D192, T206 and gives 4.9 ± 0.5% (r6; reused as the apo row of the 2017 JACS Table 1). The kex values agree within error (790 ± 60 versus 860 ± 120 s-1).

Dynamic domain 1 and hinge, apo 25 °C: Table 1 of the 2009 paper gives kex 790 ± 70 s-1, pB 0.4 ± 0.1%, while its text reports a collective fit of 990 ± 110 s-1 with pB < 0.3% and calls the result semi-quantitative (r1). The apo methyls in the same region (L219, I231) give 3,890 ± 29 s-1, pB 0.56% (r11).

Number of apo processes: backbone data are fitted as four concerted cluster motions (r1, r4-r7), while the methyl study reports heterogeneous per-site rates and a possible three-state residue (I210), and says methyl timescales are not completely consistent with the backbone (r11).

TSA complex at 25 °C: backbone groups give 2,300-2,750 s-1 (r15) and methyls 4,247 s-1 (r13); the samples differ in ligand concentrations (60 mM Arg/6 mM ADP versus 100 mM Arg/20 mM ADP) and in KCl/Mg, so probe and sample are confounded.
questions_for_gina: Which threshold and data produced the RelaxDB ARGKIN_CPMG labels? The curator note cites Fig. 3 (Rex > 2 SD = 5 s-1, 17 residues, TROSY/anti-TROSY experiment), while the 2009 CPMG Table 1 uses ΔR2eff > 2 s-1 (34 residues), and the 2011 counts vary with temperature (33, 23, 34, 28 residues at 15-30 °C).

Every apo NMR sample used 10 mM sodium or potassium citrate at pH 6.5 with no citrate-free control, while all bound samples switched to imidazole plus 8-30 mM MgCl2. Should apo exchange be flagged as untested for citrate binding at the anionic substrate sites, and should apo-versus-bound comparisons be treated as buffer-confounded?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Untested condition, not a suspected artefact: all apo NMR data (2009 backbone CPMG and relaxation r1-r3, 2011 four-temperature CPMG r4-r7, 2010 RDCs r8-r9, 2017 methyl CPMG r11) were recorded in 10 mM sodium or potassium citrate at pH 6.5, and none of these sources reports a citrate-free control; no Limulus NMR sample used phosphate. Bound-state samples (r12-r17, r24) switched to 10 mM (d4-)imidazole with 8-30 mM MgCl2 and 1 mM DTT, so ligand and buffer change together. The apo methyl sample's DTT is 0.5 mM in the JACS Methods but 1.0 mM in SI Table S1 (r11), unresolved; the RDC sample lists no DTT or KCl. Kinetics (kcat, Ea) used tris at pH 8 with Mg and substrates, not the NMR buffer (r4-r7). Phosphate as a confound appears only in the Daphnia homolog crystals (1.8 M phosphate, phosphate in the nucleotide site; r26, r30). EDTA was used in purification only (r24).
